description: Ollama/OpenAI-compatible model server on the SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML inference engine (GGUF, KV-cache decode, WebGPU dispatch-plan capture/replay). One handler core, two transports: HTTP on desktop (drop-in for Ollama clients on :11434), MessagePort in the browser (shared/dedicated worker) - the same request/response shapes either way.
releaseNotes: v1.5.3 - The Ollama routes resolve options as Ollama does: Ollama's defaults (temperature 0.8, top_k 40, top_p 0.9), then the model's own PARAMETERs (its params layer, e.g. qwen3 temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95), then the request. A client that sends no options samples as on Ollama; it got greedy decoding before. v1.5.2 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.33 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.53: faster convolutions on small grids (desktop), one GPU wait per captured WebGPU replay, model stores that tell an unreadable sidecar from a missing one, and a WebGPU dispatch helper that loads outside a page (Node). v1.5.1 - top_k and top_p together apply both, as Ollama does (k best, then the nucleus), on batch-decoder models (qwen2, qwen3, llama); only top_k was applied before, so sampled replies of clients that send both (most Ollama clients by default) change. Session-engine models keep top_k alone. v1.5.0 - min_p, presence_penalty and repeat_last_n reach the sampler (Ollama options, OpenAI presence_penalty / min_p) on the batch-decoder engine; a session-engine model refuses them with a 400 instead of ignoring them; out-of-range values are a 400. OpenAI and Anthropic error codes follow the status (were always "not found"). v1.4.9 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.32 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.51: which models stay on the GPU is decided by SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML's ModelResidency, on the accelerator's own memory budget (KV caches and scratch counted, idle scratch given back before a model is dropped; on CUDA the driver's real free memory with a reserve), and each eviction is logged; GpuResidency is kept but obsolete; faster convolutions for the image, speech and voice models; models load whole from hosts that gzip responses. v1.4.8 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.30 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.49: models with a SentencePiece vocabulary (Llama 2, Mistral, Gemma) are tokenized correctly; the browser model cache recovers when the browser clears the storage of the site; the compiler memory of a model is freed after its first run in the browser; Float16 weights load as Q8_0 when the card is short of memory; the silent wrong results and device-loss fixes of SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.29 to 5.4.49. v1.4.7 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.15 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.28: short prompts' first token about 2.7x sooner on CUDA (about 2.2x with FastInt8Decode; long prompts and decode unchanged); WebGPU fixes for in-kernel view lengths of unaligned slices and 64-bit views and for kernels with by-value struct parameters; a DelegateSpecialization launcher no longer reused across accelerators. v1.4.6 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.13: FIXES wrong logits on CUDA for prompts over 512 tokens on models whose attention v uses a different weight type than q/k (most Q4_K_M builds; 1.4.5 / ML 5.8.11 bug, CUDA only - update). Opt-in fast int8 decode (OllamaCacheModelProvider.FastInt8Decode, host env SPAWNDEV_AI_INT8_DECODE=1): ~11% faster CUDA decode on Q4_K models at a small accuracy cost; ML 5.8.12's ~23% faster CUDA prefill. v1.4.5 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.11: faster batch-decoder decode (CUDA, qwen3:1.7b-q8_0 on an RTX 4070: 166.9 -> 182.3 tok/s at a short prompt, 141.3 -> 174.1 at 1,602 tokens; greedy text unchanged), the v projection overlapped with q/k on CUDA (graph fork/join). v1.4.4 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.6: the batch decoder regroups Q8_0 weights in place at load (same bytes, no extra memory), so Q8_0 models decode about 13% faster in the browser on WebGPU (Qwen3-1.7B Q8_0, RTX 4070: 147.4 -> 166.3 tok/s at a short prompt, measured by SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML). LoRA adapters over Q8_0 bases give the same tokens as 5.8.5. v1.4.3 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.5: Q8_0 GGUF models decode about 2x faster on CUDA through the batch decoder (qwen3:1.7b-q8_0 on an RTX 4070: 82.5 -> 164.0 tok/s at a short prompt, 71.9 -> 140.8 at 1,600 prompt tokens, greedy output unchanged), a faster Q6_K decode GEMV, a per-run output leak fixed in 23 pipelines, and an in-place LoRA adapter swap on a resident batch-decoder model now takes effect on the next decode (recorded decode steps are dropped). v1.4.2 - On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.3 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.16: faster tensor-core prefill GEMMs and flash prefill (ldmatrix) on the batch decoder, LoRA training steps 2.5x faster (llama3.1:8b 4.5 -> 1.78 s on an RTX 4070). v1.4.1 - AiChatEngine.PassObserver: each generation pass with its exact rendered prompt (token ids and text with special tokens kept), generated token ids, end-of-turn ids, the stop token that ended it, the LoRA adapter label and raw output, for training data that matches inference; AiChatEngine.TokenizeAsync / DecodeAsync; LoRA adapters: ModelRegistry.SetAdapterAsync (PEFT directory or LoraAdapterSet, either engine, swapped in place on the batch decoder). On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.2. v1.4.0 - AiMemoryEngine: memory search on the accelerator (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 + DeviceVectorIndex; 50,000 entries p95 5.6 ms on an RTX 4070 including the embed) and ConsolidateAsync (episodes into facts with provenance, conflicts superseded). OllamaModelInstaller (install a model without Ollama, models.spawndev.com then registry.ollama.ai). AiFaceEngine: face detection and recognition (YuNet + SFace) on the shared accelerator, with a face registry (introductions, Visitor N guests, expiry). Chat on the batch decoder by default (GgufEngine.Auto: qwen2 / qwen3 / llama; llama3.1:8b on an RTX 4070 at a 3.7k-token prompt: first token after 200 new tokens 204 ms, prompt 1,660 tok/s, decode 45.5 tok/s; tensor-core prefill on CUDA sm_75+). Ollama /api/chat and /api/generate report eval_count / eval_duration and the other timing fields. AiSpeakerEngine.ReleaseWorkingMemoryAsync. On SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML 5.8.1 and SpawnDev.ILGPU 5.4.15. v1.3.0 - Live words: AiStreamingSpeechEngine (Nemotron Speech Streaming 0.6B, words as they are spoken, 5.63% WER on 60 LibriSpeech clips, a 160 ms chunk in ~70 ms).
